audit.rangeBounds: Start is included; end is excluded.

console.overviewDegradedNotice: The API instance reports degraded readiness. Review dependency statuses and refresh.
console.overviewApiSourceHelp: Share these details with a developer when reporting an issue. The source commit identifies the code; compare the fingerprint with dist/build-identity.json in the expected API artifact to check the deployed build. A fingerprint alone cannot identify the source commit.
console.overviewWebSourceHelp: This ID comes from the web server that rendered these build details. Use it to identify that server’s build when investigating a rollout. It does not necessarily identify the JavaScript already loaded in this tab. The tab’s update detection uses the web build ID separately.
console.overviewPoolScope: Connections and waiting requests in this API process.
console.overviewMemoryScope: Memory used by JavaScript in the responding API process.
console.overviewDiskScope: The filesystem containing API /; not S3 or a separate uploads mount.
console.overviewIndependentSamplesHelp: Resources are independent measurements from the responding API instance; readiness can use a different sample. Refresh to obtain a new snapshot.
console.overviewNotReadyHelp: The responding API instance reports not ready. Review dependency statuses and refresh.
console.overviewBuildUnavailable: Build identity is available after an API production build.
console.overviewFilesHelp: Checks whether file storage is working by writing, reading and deleting a temporary file. Your files are not changed. If checks stop arriving, the status becomes outdated.
console.overviewFilesAccessDenied: Access was denied. Check storage credentials and write, read and delete permissions; this does not prove the storage service is down.
console.overviewFilesTimeout: The check exceeded its time limit. Check storage connectivity and response times.
console.overviewFilesMismatch: The file read back did not match the bytes written.
console.overviewFilesIoError: A file operation failed. Check the storage endpoint, mount, free space and server logs.
console.overviewFilesReadinessHelp: File monitoring runs independently of API readiness. A persistent failure can trigger monitoring alerts when a notification receiver is configured.
console.overviewReadyHelp: The responding API instance passed its readiness checks. File monitoring has its own result below.
console.overviewPoolHelp: Connections in this API process. Idle connections are reusable; waiting requests suggest the pool is busy. Waiting above the configured threshold makes this API instance not ready to serve requests. These counts do not prove database connectivity or describe other instances.
console.overviewMemoryHelp: Memory used by JavaScript in this API process. Growth across snapshots can indicate a leak. Above the configured limit the readiness memory check fails. This is not total process, container or VPS memory.
console.overviewDiskHelp: Available space on the filesystem containing / in this API instance. Low space can prevent writes; pressure includes reserved blocks. The threshold affects readiness. This is not S3 capacity or a separate uploads mount; container storage can be backed by the host filesystem.
console.overviewFilesMemory: Test memory storage; files do not survive a restart
console.overviewFilesWaiting: Waiting for the current check to finish
console.overviewFilesCostHelp: Each API/worker instance independently performs one write, one read and one delete per check. Increase the interval to reduce request costs; failures will take longer to detect. Free allowances and prices depend on your provider.

backgroundWork.title: Background work
backgroundWork.description: Read-only view of the background queues: whether work is piling up, paused or cannot be read.
backgroundWork.boardPointer: To look at the jobs themselves, open the queue board. It is view-only.
backgroundWork.scope: Figures come from the queues of the Redis configured for this API, shared by every API and worker process. They show where work is waiting, not whether workers are running.

board.noteBody: Browse queue status and job details. Retrying or deleting jobs and managing queues is not available here, and some job details are hidden.
board.disabledBody: The board is off because ENABLE_BULL_BOARD is not true in the environment of the API process. To turn it on, set ENABLE_BULL_BOARD=true in the API process environment (not in the .env file) and restart the API. Turning it on does not change what the board allows: it stays view-only.
board.unavailableTitle: Could not open the queue board
board.unavailableBody: Check that the API is available and try again.

backgroundWork.autoRefreshHelp: Refreshes about every 30 seconds while this tab is visible and online. Pausing it does not pause any queue.
backgroundWork.availableIn: {seconds, plural, one {Available in # second} other {Available in # seconds}}
backgroundWork.staleNotice: Showing data from {time}. The last refresh failed.
backgroundWork.allUnavailable: No queue could be read. Unavailable does not mean empty; check Redis and the API.
backgroundWork.pausedHint: Jobs stay waiting and are not processed until the queue is resumed.
backgroundWork.unavailableHint: Could not be read. This is not an empty queue.
backgroundWork.disabledHint: Turned off in this deployment's queue inventory. Nothing is read.
backgroundWork.delayedHint: Scheduled or retrying work. It is not necessarily a problem.
backgroundWork.failedHint: Retained failed jobs only. BullMQ trims them by age and count, so this is not a lifetime total.
backgroundWork.oldestHint: Creation age of the oldest job found in a small sample at the front of the line. A lower bound, not time spent waiting.

email.title: Email
email.description: Sends transactional email that is safe to queue. Messages with secret links are sent directly and never appear here.

default.title: Default
default.description: Extension queue for your own jobs. The starter ships no worker for it, so jobs added here wait until you add a processor.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Wake signals only. Delivery state is stored in the database, so an empty queue does not mean nothing is pending.

ai-runs.title: AI runs
ai-runs.description: Wake signals only. Run state is stored in the database, so an empty queue does not mean nothing is pending.

wake.title: Wake queue
wake.description: Wake signals only. State lives elsewhere, so an empty queue does not mean nothing is pending.
